stem: What does the "S" in USB stand for?

options.content: Serial
options.rationale: Correct: universal serial bus.

options.content: System
options.rationale: USB is the universal serial bus.

options.content: Standard
options.rationale: USB is a standard, but the S stands for serial.

options.content: Storage
options.rationale: USB connects many devices besides storage.

explanation: USB = universal serial bus: data is sent serially, one bit at a time.

stem: Which port is designed to carry high-definition video **and** sound to a monitor or television through one cable?

options.content: HDMI
options.rationale: Correct: HDMI carries digital video and audio together.

options.content: Ethernet
options.rationale: Ethernet connects a computer to a network.

options.content: Audio jack
options.rationale: An audio jack carries sound only.

options.content: VGA
options.rationale: VGA is an older analogue port for video only.

explanation: HDMI carries high-definition video and sound in one digital cable.

stem: What happens first when a new device is plugged into a USB port?

options.content: The user must restart the computer
options.rationale: USB devices can be connected while the computer is on.

options.content: The data is sent in parallel
options.rationale: USB sends data serially.

options.content: The computer detects that a device is connected
options.rationale: Correct: detection comes first, then identification and the driver.

options.content: The device's battery is charged fully
options.rationale: Charging can happen, but detection comes first.

explanation: Sequence: device detected → device identified → driver loaded or installed → data transmitted serially.

stem: Why does a USB flash drive not need its own power supply?

options.content: It stores enough charge to last for years
options.rationale: Flash drives have no battery; they take power from the port.

options.content: Flash memory needs no power to read or write
options.rationale: Reading and writing need electrical power.

options.content: The driver provides the power it needs
options.rationale: A driver is software and cannot supply power.

options.content: The USB cable or port supplies power to it
options.rationale: Correct: USB carries power as well as data.

explanation: USB supplies power to connected devices, which is one of its benefits.

options.content: Devices are detected automatically
options.rationale: That is a benefit (plug and play).

options.content: It can supply power to devices
options.rationale: That is a benefit.

options.content: The maximum cable length is only a few metres
options.rationale: Correct: longer cables make the signal unreliable.

options.content: Most computers have USB ports
options.rationale: That is a benefit: it is an industry standard.

explanation: USB drawbacks: limited cable length, slower older versions, limited power, several connector types.

stem: A pupil plugs headphones into a computer, but no sound comes out. The volume is turned up and not muted. What should be checked next?

options.content: That the computer's processor is fast enough
options.rationale: Processor speed does not stop sound playing.

options.content: That the headphones are plugged into the Ethernet port
options.rationale: Audio plugs do not fit an Ethernet port.

options.content: That the printer is switched on
options.rationale: The printer has nothing to do with sound.

options.content: That the plug is in the audio output jack, not the microphone jack
options.rationale: Correct: a plug in the wrong jack is a common simple fault.

explanation: Check the simple things first: the correct port, a firm connection, power, then the driver and settings.
hints: Troubleshooting starts with the simplest causes: cables and ports.

stem: A new USB 3 external drive is plugged into an older USB 2 port. What is the most likely result?

options.content: It is not recognised and does not work
options.rationale: USB is backward compatible, so it still works.

options.content: It works at the slower USB 2 speed
options.rationale: Correct: USB is backward compatible, at the older speed.

options.content: It works at the full USB 3 transfer speed
options.rationale: The older port limits the speed.

options.content: It damages the older USB port
options.rationale: Backward compatibility is designed in.

explanation: USB is backward compatible, so the drive works, but data moves at the speed of the older port.
hints: Think about backward compatibility and which part limits the speed.

stem: USB sends data one bit at a time along its data wires.
explanation: True. USB is a serial interface.

stem: A device driver is a cable that connects a peripheral to the computer.
explanation: False. A device driver is software that lets the operating system communicate with a particular device.

stem: Match each device to the port it is most likely to use.

left.content: Projector showing a video with sound

explanation: HDMI for video and sound; Ethernet for wired networks; audio jacks for headphones and speakers; USB for flash drives and many other peripherals.

stem: Complete the description of how a USB device is set up.

payload.template: When a device is plugged in, the computer {{blank:a}} it and identifies the type of device. The operating system then loads the correct device {{blank:b}}. Data is sent {{blank:c}}, one bit at a time.

explanation: Detect → identify → load driver → transmit serially.

stem: Give the term for a computer detecting a newly connected device and setting it up automatically.
explanation: Plug and play: the device is detected and its driver loaded without manual installation.

stem: A technician must connect 30 computers in a laboratory. Each computer needs a keyboard, a mouse and a webcam, all connected by USB. How many USB ports are needed in total?
Explain how the USB interface is used to transmit data from a newly connected device to a computer. [4]

points.description: The computer detects that a device has been connected
The device is identified (it tells the computer what type of device it is)
The appropriate device driver is loaded / installed automatically
Data is transmitted serially (one bit at a time)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: When the device is plugged in, the computer detects it and the device identifies itself. The operating system loads or installs the correct driver. Data is then sent serially, one bit at a time, along the USB cable.

hints: Start from the moment the device is plugged in.
Mention the driver and how bits are sent.

stem: A printer connected by USB to an office computer in Masvingo will not print. Describe **four** checks the technician should make. [4]

points.description: Check the printer is switched on and has power (and paper/ink)
Check the USB cable is firmly connected at both ends
Try a different USB port or a different cable
Check the printer driver is installed / the correct printer is selected as default (or restart the computer)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Check the printer is on and has paper; check the cable is firmly plugged in at both ends; try another port or cable; check the driver is installed and the printer is selected, then restart if needed.

explanation: Power, cable, port, driver/settings: simplest causes first.

stem: A school in Bulawayo is buying keyboards, mice and external drives for its new computer laboratory. The supplier recommends USB devices.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which type of transmission does USB use?

options.content: Parallel
options.rationale: USB is serial.

options.content: Serial
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Simplex only
options.rationale: USB can send both ways.

options.content: Analogue
options.rationale: USB is digital.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **three** benefits of using USB devices in the laboratory.

points.description: Industry standard: the devices fit almost any computer
Plug and play: detected and drivers installed automatically
Supplies power, so keyboards, mice and drives need no separate power supply (or backward compatible)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: USB is a standard, so devices work in any computer; devices are detected and set up automatically; the port supplies power, so no extra power supplies are needed.

points.description: Maximum cable length is only a few metres
Older versions are slow / limited power for large devices / several connector types needing adapters

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cables can only be a few metres long, and older USB versions transfer data slowly.

explanation: USB: serial; standard, plug and play, power; short cables and slower older versions.
hints: Drawbacks: length, speed of older versions.

stem: Tendai is setting up a computer for a church office in Harare. He has a monitor, speakers, a printer, a network cable and a flash drive.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Match each device to the most suitable port.
parts.explanation: HDMI video, audio jack sound, Ethernet network, USB storage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe the steps Tendai should follow to set up the new printer.

points.description: Connect the printer to the computer with the correct (USB) cable and connect its power
Switch it on so the computer detects it
Install the driver if it is not installed automatically (from the manufacturer's disc or website)
Set it as the default printer and print a test page

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Connect the printer's USB cable and power, switch it on, let the computer detect it and install the driver (from the manufacturer if needed), then set it as default and print a test page.

explanation: Choose the right port; connect, power, driver, configure, test.
hints: Match each device to the port designed for its type of data.
